name: Switch
summary: A switch is a checkbox that takes effect the moment it is flipped. Use it for a setting that applies immediately, never for one that waits for a Save button. It is drawn as a track and a thumb so the state reads from position as well as color, because color alone is not a cue.
demoNote: Flip Order alerts and the confirmation arrives politely, without renaming the control. Tab to the locked Audit logging switch: it still takes focus and still says why, which is what aria-disabled buys over disabled.

contract.useWhen: An on/off that applies immediately, with the thumb as the second cue.
keyboard: native: one stop per switch — the drawn track is not focusable
native: submits the form if there is one. It never toggles
failureModes: the track color as the only cue, so the state is carried by color alone (SC 1.4.1)
role=switch reached for by default — it announces inconsistently in older JAWS
a switch that needs a Save button, which should have been a checkbox
the real input hidden with display:none, which removes the keyboard route
disabled rather than aria-disabled when the person needs to know why
api: AC.createSwitch(root, options) -> { set, state, refresh, input, destroy }
